ranked.headline: Pretrained encoders and structured priors refine molecular and protein representations
ranked.summary: Pretrained chemical and protein language models are now routinely combined with graph and knowledge priors in drug and molecule prediction.

ranked.headline: Objective-driven generative models for RNA, peptide, and protein conformational design
ranked.summary: Preprints from January–February 2026 apply objective-driven conditioning of pretrained generative models to RNA, peptide, and protein conformational tasks.

ranked.headline: Structured priors and network knowledge guide single-cell and omics inference models
ranked.summary: Encoding biological structure directly in inference objectives, rather than correcting outputs afterward, is emerging across single-cell and omics tasks.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking exposes dataset-specific limits of genomic variation computational methods
ranked.summary: Explicit ground-truth and benchmark validation now tests variant, repeat, and noncoding constraint methods on defined datasets.

ranked.headline: Viral sequence variation linked to variant and antigenic classification
ranked.summary: Epistatic coupling, antigenic mapping, and host-adaptation analysis are now being applied to SARS-CoV-2 and influenza genomic data.

ranked.headline: Histology-informed graph models sharpen spatial transcriptomic domain identification
ranked.summary: Spatial omics increasingly pairs expression with histology and coordinates, letting tissue morphology guide spatial and molecular inference.

ranked.headline: Pretrained genomic models are being adapted to regulatory and variant prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Parameter-efficient transfer and explainable modeling are now being applied to regulatory genomics models spanning sequence to transcriptome.

ranked.headline: Browser-based platforms expose GWAS, QTL, and network analyses for interactive reuse
ranked.summary: Recent preprints package harmonized GWAS and QTL summary statistics and multi-omics workflows into interactive tools for precision medicine.

ranked.headline: Sequence and structure models target protein disorder, binding interfaces and dynamics
ranked.summary: Per-residue disorder predictors, interface fingerprints and membrane-binding models now draw on protein language models and MD simulations.

ranked.headline: Learned models bridge histology, omics, and single-cell data for biological prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair deep models with pathway benchmarks, knowledge graphs, and causal cell models to move prediction toward interpretable targets.

ranked.headline: Frameworks standardize spatial, bulk and single-cell omics analysis for reproducibility
ranked.summary: Interactive front ends and integrated Python and R platforms now connect omics analysis with browsing, simulation and spatial data formats.

ranked.headline: Deep learning quantifies cell and tissue phenotypes from microscopy and tomography
ranked.summary: Recent deep-learning imaging pipelines now extract quantitative phenotypes from live cells, organoids, osteocyte networks, and whole kidneys.

ranked.headline: Draft genomes and orthology tools link gene repertoire change to ecology across taxa
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair new draft genomes with orthology platforms that tie gene content to ecology and pathogenicity.

ranked.headline: Computational models link protease dynamics, substitutions, and HIV resistance evolution
ranked.summary: Recent work couples AlphaFold2 ensembles, alignment-based substitution detection, and resistance forecasting to probe HIV protease evolution.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models infer selection and mutation from sparse genomic and single-cell data
ranked.summary: Cross-sectional single-cell and sparse genomic snapshots now support model-based inference of selection and accumulation parameters.

ranked.headline: Deep models predict cancer prognosis and leukemia subtypes from omics and clinical data
ranked.summary: Semi-supervised and multi-task networks are extending outcome prediction to unlabeled cohorts and multimodal pediatric leukemia data.

ranked.headline: Structural priors and hierarchies are being built into biomolecular deep learning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and two publications embed ontologies, hierarchies, and physical constraints into neural models for biomolecular prediction.

ranked.headline: Software tools improving reliability of RNA-seq quality control and normalization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add scalable normalization, pipeline QC flagging, and assay benchmarks that bear on RNA-seq analytical reliability.

ranked.headline: Genome architecture and mobile elements shape sex chromosome and symbiotic evolution
ranked.summary: Assembly-scale genomes now resolve neo-Y formation, Starship transposon compartments, and mitogenome recombination across fungi, insects, and plants.

ranked.headline: Reinspecting existing transcriptomic data to resolve transcript and coding annotations
ranked.summary: Recent reanalysis of existing transcriptomic and Ribo-Seq evidence is resolving annotation disputes over coding status and open reading frames.

ranked.headline: Structured models yield analytic thresholds for epidemic and community dynamics
ranked.summary: Explicit heterogeneity in hosts, behavior, and interaction networks is being encoded into reduced analytic objects that predict outcomes.

ranked.headline: Annotation tool choice alters repeat, transcript, and gene presence-absence calls
ranked.summary: Recent work benchmarks or redesigns genome and transcript annotation tools, showing that method choice shapes annotation outcomes.

ranked.headline: Interpretable learned representations of individual brain structure and function
ranked.summary: Recent preprints replace fixed parcellations with atlas-free voxel, graph, and surface-based models of individual brain anatomy and function.

ranked.headline: Resource-efficient tools and bias-aware benchmarks for microbial and viral genomics
ranked.summary: Preprints and publications pair memory-efficient implementations with systematic tests of upstream technical bias in microbial and viral data.

ranked.headline: Single-cell RNA-seq methods infer tumor clonal structure and ecDNA dynamics
ranked.summary: ecSingle and SCANBIT apply pseudobulk and allelic-imbalance logic to scRNA-seq for clonal and ecDNA inference at single-cell resolution.

ranked.headline: Sparse and multi-contributor aDNA sampling biases kinship and selection inference
ranked.summary: Recent work benchmarks selection and kinship inference on sparse ancient DNA data, where sampling design determines inferential accuracy.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved assemblies and pangenomes sharpen variant and structural analysis
ranked.summary: Phased assemblies and pangenome graphs now resolve haplotypes across human, cattle, apple and clover genomes for variant and trait analysis.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and regulatory profiling resolves disease-linked cell states
ranked.summary: Single-cell atlases and multi-omics frameworks resolve beta-cell stress trajectories and regulatory regions across aging, diabetes and neurodevelopment.

ranked.headline: Conformational ensembles link disordered protein sequence to aggregation propensity
ranked.summary: Recent simulations quantify Aβ monomer ensembles, IDP stickiness, and temperature-dependent phase behavior with explicit free-energy methods.

ranked.headline: Harmonized knowledgebases and atlases unify biomarker, drug-response and toxicity data
ranked.summary: Standardizing heterogeneous drug, biomarker, and toxicity data across studies requires FAIR, harmonized resources linking molecular and clinical evidence.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking LC-MS platforms and search tools for proteomics depth and quantitation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers evaluate LC-MS acquisition workflows, spectral search engines, and QC software for proteomic measurement performance.

ranked.headline: MD simulations dissect allosteric coupling between ligands, partners and their targets
ranked.summary: Recent MD studies pair machine-learning analysis with simulation to define allosteric switches in TCR-pMHC and p53 systems.

ranked.headline: Network-level drug-target mapping spanning predictive modeling and curated databases
ranked.summary: Three January 2026 items map multi-target drug-target relationships across herbal, JAK2/GLP-1R, and sodium channel contexts.

ranked.headline: Faster read mapping, alignment, and community detection via kernel-level redesign
ranked.summary: Runtime bottlenecks in read mapping, sequence alignment, and graph analysis motivate hardware and algorithmic reengineering of core computational kernels.

ranked.headline: Software tools link atomic structures to force analysis and coarse-grained self-assembly
ranked.summary: Automated analysis and coarse-grained modeling tools now connect atomic structures to steered dynamics and self-assembly simulations.

ranked.headline: Transposon-derived promoters and piRNA tools map regulatory sequence across genomes
ranked.summary: A 26,056-element atlas of TE-derived TSSs shows that younger elements drive stronger, focused promoter activity across human tissues.

ranked.headline: Stochastic and growth models of cell-state and population dynamics across three systems
ranked.summary: Preprints now link cell-cycle-linked state inheritance to drug resistance and argue for time-resolved designs in preclinical studies.

ranked.headline: Computational tools link microbial metabolites to metabolomics and microbiome function
ranked.summary: Community knowledgebases and functional metabolomics workflows now connect untargeted LC-MS/MS data to microbial metabolic models and drug transformations.

ranked.headline: Computational methods quantify spatial and morphological structure in single-cell omics
ranked.summary: Recent methods target 3D, single-molecule, and morphological spatial data, extending spatial inference beyond spot-level expression analysis.

ranked.headline: Molecular dynamics links Complex I hydration and proton transport to disease mutations
ranked.summary: Atomistic and multiscale simulations quantify how hydration connectivity and quinone binding shape Complex I proton transport and LHON pathogenicity.
